answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor: an agent first posts a hashed commitment of its identity, bonded with stake, and must wait past a fixed horizon of several epochs before it may reveal and transact. A sybil farmer thus has to pre-fund every fake name and leave that capital idle until reveal, so cost scales with headcount and time, not clever scripting. Like a falcon holding its circle before the dive, honest agents lose little by waiting; an attacker spinning up thousands of names ties up stake as dear as saffron per identity, and correlated reveals get slashed.
